chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yasir the servant, from al-Ridha (peace be upon him), who said:

'There is no problem with drinking water abundantly with food, but do not be excessive with it other than with food.' And he said: 'Do you not see that if a man ate the likes of this' — and he gathered both his hands neither joining them together nor separating them — 'then did not drink water over it, his stomach would burst?'

key_terms.كَثْرَةِ شُرْبِ الْمَاءِ: drinking water abundantly — the subject being ruled permissible when with food
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem/objection — a standard jurisprudential phrase indicating permissibility
key_terms.مَعِدَة: stomach — the organ at risk of harm without water after a large meal

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to drink large amounts of water with food according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) provides dietary guidance permitting drinking water freely with meals while cautioning against excessive water intake at other times. He uses a physical demonstration — cupping his hands to show the volume of food — to illustrate that water is physiologically necessary after a substantial meal, as failing to drink afterward could cause the stomach to burst. This hadith reflects the Imams' tradition of offering practical health wisdom to their companions.
